message:
A three-blade fixed-pitch upwind Horizontal-Axis Wind Turbine (HAWT) with 40 cm diameter fits the 45 cm cube and follows competition-winner practice. I read the Kansas State University Technical Design Report for the 2021 U.S. Department of Energy Collegiate Wind Competition (E2) which states the final turbine was a 3-bladed, fixed-pitch, direct-drive assembly with passive centrifugal Revolutions Per Minute (RPM) control, and I adopt that layout for the tri-star rotor (C1) plus rigid hub (C3).

For low-wind production I use thin low-Reynolds sections with Power Coefficient (Cp) 0.34 at Tip-Speed Ratio (TSR) 6. I read the Design of Small Horizontal Axis Wind Turbine for Low Wind Speed Rural Applications (E3) which found the SD7080 airfoil best with maximum lift-to-drag ratio 46.3 and optimum Cp 0.34 at TSR 6, and I apply it in the SD7080 rotor (C2); with 40 cm diameter the available wind power (E9) 9.62 W at 5 m/s and (E10) 102 W at 11 m/s give shaft power (E11) 3.27 W at 5 m/s and (E12) 34.7 W at 11 m/s, about a phone charger, which is plausible for start-up at 5 m/s.

Speed and load set survival and braking. The same TSR 6 gives rotor speed (E14) 1.43e+03 RPM at 5 m/s and (E13) 3.15e+03 RPM at 11 m/s for direct-drive matching (C4), while wind dynamic load scale (E15) 37.3 N at 22 m/s is about 3.80 kg weight, easily carried to the post but requiring stall limiting; I read (E3) shows soft stall in 4 to 9 deg angle range and (E2) shows unloaded overspeed near 4300 RPM, so I add soft-stall sections (C7) to cap thrust and speed.

Not ready, because rotor and hub concepts are posted but selection, nacelle interface, and bench test for power curve still need Manager decision.
